title: Does the sharded duplicate-name check pull further ahead with more targets and threads?
body:
`refuse_repeated_names` in `nail/src/io/records.rs` refuses an input fasta or hmm file that repeats a record name. It hashes every name in parallel, then splits the records into one shard per rayon thread by name hash. Each shard checks its records with its own `HashSet`, so a repeated name lands twice in one shard.

On 2,455,940 mgy targets at 8 threads on the 16-core box, with a warm page cache, the check alone took:

| variant | seconds |
|---|---|
| binary search per record over libsail's name index, one thread | 2.37 to 2.45 |
| the same binary search, 8 threads | 0.23 to 0.24 |
| one `HashSet`, one thread | 0.15 to 0.16 |
| `HashSet` per shard, 8 threads, the one nail uses | 0.04 to 0.05 |

The comment on the shard loop claims the gap should grow with the number of targets and the number of threads. Nobody has measured that. The variants are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-serial-overhead/index-split/src/bin/check.rs` on the 16-core box, run as `check <variant> <fasta> <threads>`, with variant one of `bsearch-1`, `bsearch-t`, `hash-1`, `hash-t`.

## Proposal

Run the four variants on the 48-thread box, on several MGnify shards concatenated to well past 2.4M targets, at 8, 16, 32 and 48 threads. If the claim holds, the issue closes with the table. If it does not, the comment changes to match what was measured.

## Open

- Peak memory of the sharded variant, which holds one `HashSet` per shard at once.
